name: St. Louis Aquarium
note: When I started volunteering at the Seattle Aquarium, I was told that Seattle had one of the best volunteering programs in the country. I definitely still believe this, but the St. Louis Aquarium definitely competes! I was impressed! And I was the only person there, so there were a handful of people staring at me the whole time.

name: Vancouver Aquarium
note: The first time I came here, we paid for parking and had to renew it over and over again. We must've been there for five hours. I remember finding a new part of the aquarium right before we were about to go, so I'm not even sure we saw the whole thing. I came back with some friends later and once again, I ran out of time! Still my favorite aquarium to visit.

name: Point Defiance Zoo and Aquarium
note: When I was at the peak of my aquarium volunteering, I got to go to a joint Seattle Aquarium and Point Defiance event called the Youth Ocean Conservation Summit. I was the only Seattle volunteer to drive down for it! It was a fun event and they were going to alternate to have the Seattle Aquarium host it the following year. Then, COVID happened.

name: Seattle Aquarium
note: What is there to say! I love this place! What first got me to volunteer was some friend-of-a-friend bumping into us at the library and telling us to volunteer here. For some reason, we listened to him. I started at the aquarium a very quiet kid. I grew into myself here. I may seem confident and charismatic today, but that has been the outcome of the gradual and intentional whittling towards that here.

name: Museum of History & Industry
note: When I was trying to figure out when I first visited this museum, it turns out, I wanted to go here pretty bad! There were a lot of texts about this place. After visiting, we walked around SLU a handful. I had never done that before!

name: Burke Museum
note: For the IB diploma, we had some cultural assignment for our theory of knowledge class. I did it elsewhere, then visited this museum with a friend later. Life changing experience! I switched my assignment so I could write about this place. It's a fun mix of natural history and Native American art and history. One piece of art was a Dorito bag with some other flair, emphasizing how Native Americans need to not be treated as a historical relic. That has always stuck with me.

name: Museum of Pop Culture
note: One of the first hangouts with my future best friend was here. MoPop + Cultural fest + Pacific Science Center + TeenTix. Best $10 you'll ever spend. I can't lie, I have definitely taken other people on that Seattle day itinerary. Don't tell me not to repeat dates! I have fun dates!

name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
note: Some things in Seattle Center are things I would go to constantly. It's not like I wouldn't come out here. This, however, is one of those things that I never really did as a local. Too expensive.

name: Pacific Science Center
note: When I was way younger, we used to have this annual event where we would get to have a sleepover at the Pacific Science Center. One year, we brought my best friend in as my sibling. Oops! We slept in the little kids play area, and we weren't all that sleepy. Definitely got some hushes and shushes all night.

name: Theo Chocolate
note: I found out recently that Theo Chocolate merged with another company and no longer make their chocolate in Seattle anymore. That was like, their whole thing to me. I'm not sure if I'll get a Theo chocolate again.

name: Salmon Days 50th Anniversary
note: When I first started collecting pins, I wanted to fill my Seattle Aquarium lanyard with pins from other aquariums I had visited. The first pin I collected for that was the Waikiki Aquarium. I immediately decided to break my aquarium-only rule to collect this pin. 50th year! I love this pin. Having moved away from home in Sammamish, telling people about Salmon Days brings me back home.

name: Cougar Mountain Zoo
note: For the longest time, I thought this was the Woodland Park Zoo. Thinking about it, I don't actually think I've ever been to the Woodland Park Zoo, Seattle's main zoo. I actually haven't been back here either. What happened?

name: Funko HQ
note: Funkos really had their moment in 2020 at some point. I remember first seeing them at a bookstore, selecting the couple characters from an IP that I only barely watched to purchase. I'm not sure why I bought them if I didn't really care for them. We went here and I started collecting Wall-E Funkos. Thinking about it, maybe I should start a Wall-E page for this website!

name: Oregon Coast Aquarium
note: At some point, I finally got comfortable at the Seattle Aquarium. For like $20, they took us on a weekend trip down to the Oregon coast. That was one of the first times I actually enjoyed a long 5+ hour drive, meeting, introducing, and getting close with the five other people in the van. The whole weekend was such a good trip. I got to become really close to some people I never would have and I'm really fond of all those new friends today.

name: Tillamook Creamery
note: I have been to the Tillamook creamery twice. The first time, I saw this pin, and decided that it wasn't an aquarium pin thus preventing me from buying it for my aquarium lanyard. Then, I thought about the pin for three years. Why didn't I buy this pin? It was such a cute pin! What have I done? Letting my made-up rules interfere with my happiness? So three years later on another road trip, I made sure we'd come back and I bought my long lost favorite pin.

name: Multnomah Falls
note: Before moving away from the Pacific Northwest, I was a little spoiled and unknowing of how boring nature could make itself. When I first saw Multnomah Falls, I thought it was rather unremarkable. I've seen two waterfalls before! And bigger ones. And closer ones. We drove all this way for this? Silly little me.

name: Powell's City of Books
note: On this trip to Portland, I visited the Portland Farmers Market and thought to myself, wow! This is awesome! I wish Seattle had something like this. Then, I got home and remembered the existence of Pike Place.

name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
note: Monterey Bay Aquarium is the biggest aquarium on the west coast. At the Seattle Aquarium, I had always looked on fondly about it because so much of the info and facts and research was coming out of Monterey Bay Aquarium. When I finally went, I got so tunnel visioned on going to the aquarium and completely forgot to spend time looking into the bay itself! I let my love for aquariums supersede my love for the ocean.

name: California Academy of Sciences
note: I'm pretty sure I went to this museum when I was really young, maybe 10 years old. We ran out of time here but I remember getting completely sucked into the physics section. All of the demos were so cool to see. When I went back, 10 years later, unsurprisingly, they updated their exhibitions. Updating the version of the museum I saw to the real version ahead of me was hard.

name: Steinhart Aquarium at CAS
note: When I was road tripping from Seattle to San Diego, we stopped in Monterey to see the Monterey Bay Aquarium. Between my friend and I, I was the big aquarium nerd and she was going because I wanted to go so bad. The next day, we planned to go to the California Academy of Sciences. Lo and behold, massive aquarium below its surface! She wanted to spend no time down there.

name: Heal the Bay Aquarium
note: This was a really small aquarium. So much so that I'm not entirely certain that I'd buy the pin nowadays. So small, in fact, that they only sell buttons! I have an issue with buttons. They're not the same! If I can make it myself, it loses its special edge. I'm not sure if that's fair actually...

name: Birch Aquarium
note: Oh, the Birch Aquarium. What do I have to say? I started volunteering here because I was bored and didn't know what to do in college. I was urged to apply for a role and so I did! Except I didn't apply for the right one. Instead, I got to be the student volunteer coordinator! A much better job if I do say so myself. So many good memories here, I cried when I had my last day. I took a leap of faith, away from the aquarium, and towards my data science life.

name: Shark Reef Aquarium
note: Every once in a while I would find myself in Las Vegas before I turned 21. I'm not entirely sure why because it felt like there wasn't all that much to do. Imagine my surprise when I learned there was an aquarium! On the strip! When I went, I forgot to buy the pin, so I had a friend who visited later buy the pin for me. I didn't think I'd be back in Vegas any time soon. Look where we are now.

name: OdySea Aquarium
note: I've been to so many aquariums on the Pacific coast that I have basically organized them into two categories, Pacific coast aquariums, and others. Usually I'm pretty good at remembering what's featured in those other aquariums. This one, not so much. I remember that instead of a mirror in the bathroom, it pointed directly into the big tank. That was cool.

name: Musical Instrument Museum
note: At some point in high school, around 2019, I saw this museum featured in a YouTube video I was watching and I thought it was the coolest place in the world. I looked it up and realized it was in some random city that I'd probably find difficult to go visit, so I forgot all about it. Lo and behold, my sister decides to go college in Phoenix and, from the ashes, this museum rises for my viewing pleasure. It is such a fun museum! One of my favorites.

name: L'Aquàrium de Barcelona
note: On this day in Barcelona, I was on a trip with my parents but nobody wanted to come to the aquarium with me. Honestly, good for everyone involved, since I spend way more time in an aquarium than most everyone else. Also on this day, I walked maybe 30,000 steps around the whole city and contemplated hopping on the train to Madrid for the evening. Wouldn't that have been fun! Might've worried them a bit.

name: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya
note: When traveling, my dad is a big time walker and adventurer. I like to think that I am too, but with him, it might seem like I'm not at all. We must have walked three or four miles just to get to this museum. Fortunately for me, my girlfriend might be an even bigger walker-traveler so I have a lot of steps in store.

name: Sagrada Família
note: Please don't laugh at me for what I'm going to say next. When I read about Barcelona, I knew about Catalonia and it's political relationship with the rest of Spain. This was my idea of Barcelona. What wasn't in my idea of Barcelona is apparently the main attraction of Barcelona, oops! Now imagine my shock when I'm looking up into the heavens.

name: Park Güell
note: When we visited the Park Güell, it was a hot summer day in Spain. Like, hot-hot. And this is an outdoor park. I didn't fare so well in the sun.

name: Casa Batlló
note: When it comes to art, I don't know a whole lot, but I love postwar modernism. I hadn't heard of Gaudí prior to this trip and seeing his work was such a surreal experience. He takes all of these ideas that I've seen before many times and makes them organic and living. It's like he injected cancerous cells into the modernism I was familiar with, reproducing and growing until you had a living piece of furniture. I loved it.

name: 37th America's Cup
note: About one month before this trip I was in my apartment watching the Copa America with my roommates. Imagine my surprise when, walking along the ocean, there's another Copa America? And it's in the water?

name: Zoo Antwerpen
note: I set out for Amsterdam on my own but I was lucky to be visiting several friends in the city. It was on this side adventure into Antwerp that I got to finally experience the true solo travel life. It was exhausting! I can only do so much walking! If you look at my camera roll from this day, you'd think I visited an aquarium because the only animals that grabbed my attention were the many beautiful fish in their one hallway of the oceans.

name: Rijksmuseum
note: When I go into big art museums, usually I don't know what pieces are housed on display. I turn a corner and there it is, the massive Rembrandt, The Night Watch. So much was going on. What a magnificent piece. I also went while they were doing work on its restoration and the museum did a great job turning it into an educational opportunity. I didn't actually mind the piece being worked on in front of me. Fun fact: on the Rijk's website, you can even look up an insanely detailed photograph of it.

name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
note: Yves Klein was introduced to me in high school. Something about the swaths of blue was magnetic. Naturally, seeing photos of his art projected onto a cheap screen wouldn't capture much, but something about the idea hooked me. I put this thought into the back of my head. A couple years later at the Stedelijk, from down the hall, visible through doorways and past other pieces, glowed this blue canvas. I couldn't take my eyes off of it. The color is deep, flat, rich, simple. I walk away and return like it fed me. It feeds me.

name: Van Gogh Museum
note: Pin with 0 visits? Square that circle, huh? I went into the gift shop and bought the pin before realizing that it was not the gift shop for the Rijks museum. Then it closed when I was trying to go afterwards. Awkward.

name: Keukenhof
note: Sometimes, I let my frugal side take over a little more than it should. At the end of this trip, I must've been scared to look at my checking account, having drained it for my first big trip on my own. I fought the urge. I took the day long trip and it was so worth it! Seeing the flower fields and wonderful tulip art in the motherland!

name: Pompeii
note: They said it was a city frozen in time. I doubted them and then I arrived and they were right. I need to trust the internet.

name: Manila Ocean Park
note: I keep making this mistake of going to aquariums with other people, particularly my sister. I can spend many hours in aquariums. Her? One hour is pushing it.

name: National Museum of Anthropology
note: This trip to the Philippines was supposed to be a return-to-the-motherland moment for my sister and I, but for reasons beyond our control, our mom wasn't able to make it. It was a great trip, don't get me wrong, but my Filipina mom not being there meant it ended up being a strange time. Anyways...

name: National Museum of Fine Arts
note: Spoliarium. Spo-li-ar-i-um. Spoliarium.

name: Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary
note: In Bohol, we went to a couple of animal-based places. There is a certain level of commercialization of animals that I, aquarium lover, am uncomfortable with. This tarsier sanctuary was definitely on the better side, but how much of it is smoke and mirrors? I'm not entirely sure. I balance my own relationship between zoos and ethics. Fish? Easy. Mammals and cetaceans? A little harder. Again, this sanctuary seemed fine, but what do I know?

name: National Archaeological Museum
note: When it comes to old stuff humans have made, I (and museums) get to play this fun game deciding whether or not I'm going to consider the ancient vases and textiles a part of an art museum or something else. I'm counting these as art museums, but I could see an argument that archeological museum means not art.

name: Acropolis Museum
note: Most impactful to me is that this is the home of five of the caryatids of the Erechtheion, with a tasteful absence for the sixth that the British Museum has yet to return. On March 21st, 2025, the sun finally set on the British Empire, so anything's possible now.

name: Herakleidon Museum
note: On our family Seattle days when my sister and I were much younger, we would split up and I would go to the Pacific Science Center and my sister would go to the Seattle Children's Museum. She must've been 3-4 years old. I don't know if she ever graduated to going to PacSci, or if we just stopped going as much later. She had a great time in this sciency-mathy museum, though. It was the only one she wanted to go to.

name: Maui Ocean Center
note: I remember vividly having gone to this aquarium on Maui, though I have zero recollection of when I was on Maui. Obviously, I had to have been to Maui, but I only remember going once when I visited Haleakala. Maybe it was the same trip? I thought those were done at very different ages though. I may never find out.

name: Waikīkī Aquarium
note: I used to come here all the time! Possibly more than the Seattle Aquarium, for a time. This was my childhood aquarium. I remember the audio devices, how big they were in my hand. I think that's all done through the phone now. This whole place felt huge.

name: Honolulu Zoo
note: Putting this all together and I'm realizing, I haven't been here in ages. Just like the Waikīkī Aquarium, this was my childhood zoo. My parents used to buy a family membership to take me and my cousins in even though we would only go once on our trip. They had these monkeys that would scare me since they would just yell at whoever walked by. I should go back.

name: Bishop Museum
note: One time, they had a temporary exhibit that was a bunch of famous guitars. Me being 10ish meant that none of these famous musicians were actually real people to me. I actually have no idea how the music world existed in my head. Who's Sting? Kurt Cobain? Elvis? I might've known about Elvis.

name: Hawaii Army Museum
note: In high school, whenever we would write papers for American history, we would be given a time period to select an event from. I kept choosing Hawaiian history for these. I think I wrote three papers. One on the overthrow of Queen Lili'uokalani, a second on the impact of military presence during WWII, and a third on the transition from a plantation-based economy to a tourism-based economy. Unfortunately, I remember nothing and I have zero desire to read my old HS papers.

name: Kualoa Ranch
note: The first time I ever went to a rodeo was in Hawaii on the Big Island. Weird, right? Not the south, not a big traveling rodeo, a Fourth of July rodeo with horses from other ranches on the island. I forget that there exist these large families that own swaths of land all around the islands. I even wrote a paper on that history too.

name: Lion Coffee
note: My uncle might have been the one to introduce me to nicer coffees, teaching me about single origin coffees and the differences in flavor between light and dark roasts. It wasn't a far leap, then, to try and find Hawaii's crown coffee: 100% Kona coffee. I'm not actually sure if Lion is the best roaster, but they are certainly iconic.

name: Faneuil Hall
note: The older I get, the easier it is to romanticize this trip we took right before college. It was our senior trip after graduating high school spending a week between New York and Boston. Of the four of us, two went to college in Boston so we dropped them off and flew home a little lighter. It was my first time in both cities, such a bittersweet way to end summer, and even had the last date with my high school girlfriend on our last night in Boston. One of those rose-tinted high school memories.

name: The Andy Warhol Museum
note: I was in Pittsburgh to present my first first-authored paper! I really loved Pittsburgh. That weekend gave me every season. Some rain, some snow, some crisp February sun, it was lovely. The downtown is so beautiful and the bridges and rivers make the skyline so artistic. Oh right, about the Warhol Museum. I made a friend during the conference and we went together. It felt like we were clones of each other.

name: San Diego Zoo
note: One of the great perks of working at the Birch Aquarium was getting to go to the museums for free (zoo included). One day, when the pandas had just made their return, I went to the zoo just to stand in the panda line, do homework, see panda, go to aviary, and take a meeting. I understand I can do this with a membership too, but it's not the same!

name: San Diego Zoo Safari Park
note: For some reason, we had been putting off the safari ride all day when we went. Maybe we started off in the other direction. By the time we made it to the attraction, we caught the final ride and got to see the whole safari under golden hour as the sun set over the animals. What a perfect ending.

name: San Diego Air & Space Museum
note: I always felt like I needed to take better advantage of the fact I could get into these museums for free. The time that I tried going here, I guess they had some special event that meant they would close early and we wouldn't be able to see the rest. And I never came back!

name: Fleet Science Center
note: When I was going through a breakup, something I did for a few weeks was bus down to Balboa Park, catch a museum or two, and bus back in the afternoon in time for our intramural soccer games. The Fleet Science Center was the first of these adventures, and it was a perfect, youthful atmosphere that was able to ground me and allow me to appreciate the world once again.

name: San Diego Natural History Museum
note: I think natural history museums are so cool. To me, they're the historical version of the aquarium or zoo! So many cool animals, the bug collections are always so pretty. To my girlfriend, she sees all the taxidermied animals, and they seem to see her back. Maybe they talk to her. She doesn't like the Nat.

name: San Diego Model Railroad Museum
note: I love this museum! Balboa Park has so many gems all throughout it and this is my favorite of the bunch. Something about the hobbyists being so close and having their very own space is very endearing. I would love to have a D&D museum where I can hang out.

name: Museum of Us
note: The first time I went to this museum I was in San Diego visiting UCSD for the first time. The thing was, I had already known I wanted to go here. I knew that to be so true, that I had accepted my offer letter long before going to San Diego for the first time. This was just a trip for the sake of it.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego
note: This might be my favorite art museum in the world. Its collection is nice, no Yves Kleins, but my relationship with Anastasiya might have started here. This was our first hang out off campus, not tied to studying or going to classes, just to be with one another. There was one piece that was just a pile of square papers on the ground, and I remember Anastasiya and I chatting with the security guard as I watch her seated on the ground, folding a flower. I could get married here.

name: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
note: A couple months into officially dating, I visited Anastasiya in Dallas for this trip. Legend has it, she realized I was serious about the relationship when I made the plan to see her. I thought we were serious much sooner than that.

name: Texas Discovery Gardens
note: In this process of looking at all my pins, it seems like I have very few botanical garden pins, which is crazy because I love botanical gardens! What's up with that! Clearly, I need to go back and start getting pins from there.

name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
note: This was our very first stop on our senior trip to New York and Boston. Frankly, I don't actually remember too much about this trip, especially the New York parts. What did we do? What did we see? I think this is the only pin I have from it, so any findings will have to come from elsewhere.

name: Museum of Broadway
note: To my friends, I might be the most musical theater person they're friends with. I didn't do theater myself, which is a big alternate universe I wish I traversed, but I love theater now as a consumer. But to my family, I am the least theater person of the four. They completely clear me! My parents have been going to shows for years, my sister is a huge theater nerd, and I'm somehow the one getting dragged along.

name: The Museum of Modern Art
note: Usually I don't look up what art pieces a museum holds before I go. It makes for a fun experience turning the corner and seeing something that you've always seen through screens. Something compelled me to look it up this time though, and upon realizing what was housed within, I beelined it for the fourth floor. There it was. The Yves Klein Blue Monochrome. But it was covered in glass! It's not the same! The depth, the beauty, the allure, all blocked by a pane of glass and the reflection of the ceiling. Free her!

name: Six
note: We land in New York as a trip for my birthday and little did I know, I was going to have little say in the activities we were going to do. Honestly for the best, Courtney convinced everyone to go see a billion broadway shows, something I probably wouldn't have done.

name: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child
note: We saw the matinee showing for this show on my birthday. I don't even think we had it planned, it happened pretty last second. It's three hours long. Later in the day went to see Book of Mormon and I got to see some old high school friends to go out with on my birthday. Our birthday, we're bday twins!

name: The Book of Mormon
note: This was supposed to be the first musical theater play I was going to see. I remember getting tickets with my friend months in advance and listening to the soundtrack and getting all excited. Those tickets were for May 2020 and we did not see it then.

name: Hadestown
note: I have some opinions on the cast that I got to see... For our viewing we saw Jordan Fisher and I was not a huge fan. I could not stand Orpheus! I thought he deserved everything bad to happen to him and I did not want to see him succeed. He came off so arrogant and manipulative, someone you'd want to punch. It was not a sweet love tragedy, it was watching a narcissist somehow keep getting passes and more and more tries. Agh! So annoying! Anyways, I missed when it came to the movie theaters. For the record, I like the songs.

name: One World Observatory
note: One day, I saw an infinity pool for the first time and finally understood the appeal. Before then, I just never stood in the right spot (and probably didn't see them all that often either). The One World Trade Center has this same effect too. One specific angle beneath the tower and it's an infinitely long tower vanishing into the sky. The rest is just your average tallest skyscraper in the US.

name: Top of the Rock
note: New York has this weird effect of letting you think some things are normal when they absolutely aren't. Public transportation, scaffolding, and skyscrapers taller than anything your city can dream of. By the time we got to the Rockefeller Center, we had seen the Empire State Building and One World Trade Center, so I was somewhat observationed out.

name: The Mob Museum
note: This Mob Museum pin was the final pin I took a picture of when first creating this page. I have a whole lot of pins! This digitization process has been a whole lot of fun trying to remember and scavenge for information about each. Funnily enough, I am completely guessing about this museum's first visit. I don't actually know.

name: The Neon Museum
note: Las Vegas being the destination for the start of my career was a happy coincidence that brought me back to my parents in a new city. I applied for this role and then suddenly, without my influence, they decided to buy a place here and snow bird after retiring! Lucky me! I feel very lucky that I don't have to go through heaven and earth just to see and hang out with my parents.

name: Omega Mart
note: This trip to Vegas fell in just the right period between the last interview for the Caesars role and me hearing back about the position. I walked around the strip and city in this weird liminal space, somewhat disappointed that I hadn't heard back and somewhat hopeful that I might. Everything looked a little different. Would this be my home? Is this the skyline I'm going to get used to? Are these the shops that I'm gonna frequent? Sometimes these liminal times happen and I try to appreciate the uncertainty and appreciate the security I have to appreciate it.

name: Atomic Museum
note: One of the first games I got on my new Xbox One was Fallout 4. I heard great things about the franchise and I had never played an RPG before, so I decided I'd try it out. The genre wasn't for me, I'd get so distracted in the open world that I'd completely forget about the plot. Years later, Fallout has an IP partnership with the Atomic Museum, and my girlfriend's the one itching and yearning to see it all! She loved it through the show! It made me smile seeing her enjoy this IP that existed in my head at a much different point in my life.

name: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix
note: So I only saw the practice, sue me! It counts! Zedd also performed and my friend and I got to the rail for that. Shoutout to my ear plugs, because otherwise, I may not have ears anymore.

name: Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta
note: Anastasiya met my parents because I accidentally invited both of them and they both decided they wanted to go. I first asked Anastasiya and it seemed like a bit of a long shot. So I told my dad because I thought he'd think it's cool, and he did! So much so, that he got the rest of my family and a cousin to all come as well. Surprise! And now Anastasiya is super down too! My family loves her so it all worked out.

name: National Museum of Nuclear Science & History
note: My dad grew up in Cold War era Hawaii with nuclear bunkers and nuclear attack drills being commonplace. This entire museum we'd walk around and go, yep, this all happened. This is what it was like, this is what the people were afraid of. Some crazy dad lore.

name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
note: There are these nice bean bag chairs in the main entrance of the museum here. One day, when I was at a conference and a little in my own head, I bumped into the SF Moma. I didn't realize it was so close! I walked in and laid on those beanbags, absorbing the ambient beauty of the building and visible artwork. For the record, I also visited this museum normally, that wasn't the only time I've been there.

name: de Young Museum
note: Something about this museum always had allured me. It has this alien presence in Golden Gate Park, especially being across the California Academy of Sciences where I have been a couple more times. The first time I visited we had little time and we only got to see the special Monet exhibit. Funny story with that Monet exhibit, I'll have to tell you later.

name: Asian Art Museum
note: One of my most entertaining sagas to embark on was when I slowly (quickly) became close friends with my Vegas bestie's bestie. Going from comment on our mutual's Instagram stories to accidentally DMing to meeting each other by going on an all day road trip with no room for awkward conversations, our getting together is one of the highlights of that year.

name: Hamilton
note: At the start of high school, there was a bit of a Hamilton craze going around, and it drove me crazy. My friends would break out into competitive lyric remembering contests (singing with an edge) and as someone who didn't get it, it irked me. I harbored this feeling into college. One of my college friends and I were chatting about Hamilton and I shared my Hamilton-kid experience. She pointed out that I not only knew all the lyrics myself, but I've also seen it in theaters and love the musical. Who's the Hamilton kid now?

name: Moulin Rouge
note: My dad always loved the Moulin Rouge version of Roxanne. I heard that version a lot and that was my full exposure to Moulin Rouge prior to seeing it in theaters. I don't remember at all what I was expecting.

name: Les Misérables
note: I might have seen Les Mis one earlier time when I was much much younger. Like, 8 or 9. It was around then, too, that I was first exposed to Les Mis and musical theater as a whole. I had seen the movie, the anniversary concert, listened to all recorded albums, and so finally getting to see it live (again) was a huge moment for me. I loved every piece of it. To me, it is the exemplar musical.

name: Chicago
note: I'm going to take credit for my friend Gaby getting into musicals. If you're reading this and I'm wrong, let me know. I have no clue what spurred us to buy tickets to this. Neither of us had a clue what this was about. The closest we had was that bit in Victorious where Trina sings Chicago. Not knowing what was going to happen was the right decision. I was beaming and giggling through the entire second act.

name: Carlsbad Caverns National Park
note: Caught this national park as a detour from our drive from Dallas to San Diego. Our first day was an ambitious 14 hours from Dallas out to Tucson and for some reason, we thought spending 3 extra hours in the middle of the day was a good idea. Turns out, it was a great idea! It split the drive up perfectly, let alone how cool the national park was. I grew up going into lava tubes from volcanic eruptions in Washington, but those were completely different! The cave was a brand new piece of nature I've ever seen.

name: Grand Canyon National Park
note: My sister had her very first breakup a couple weeks before her birthday this year. I didn't really realize how it was going until the entire family was summoned into Phoenix to celebrate her birthday with her. Took the quick drive from San Diego to Phoenix to catch them for the weekend and surprise! We're going to see the Grand Canyon! They weren't wrong. It's very grand!

name: Death Valley National Park
note: I love stargazing. I don't know what started this when I was a young 15 year old, but I guess I had an appreciation for nature early. This is great for me because I get to bring my friends stargazing for the first time and experience their newfound awe with them. Once we drove the two hours out to Death Valley to get the best view of the sky, and then I got to drive back all alone as the rest of the car slept. Zzz.

name: Tahoma National Park
note: I'm on Team Call Mount Rainier, Tahoma. Be the change you want to see! Small problem, not many actually adhere to this, so when it ever comes up, I have to trip around the name a bit. In other news, she is beautiful. It goes without saying. PNW summer is the best time of year in the best place in the US. There is nothing that tops it. The mountain peeking out, quietly reminding you of not just the trees, the water, but also the powerful mountains just a few miles away. I can't wait to go back to Washington.

name: Joshua Tree National Park
note: Came here solo once. Got lost on a trail. I didn't realize how lost I was so I couldn't start to panic. Figured it out eventually though!

name: Yosemite National Park
note: Once came here long, long ago for my grandpa's 90th birthday. I don't remember a single thing, but framed at home is this cute collage-like framed thing with cute pictures and captions over our heads. I want this musubi! You can't have it! I don't know who made it or if other family members have their own, but it's cute. I see the appeal of scrap booking.

name: Petrified Forest National Park
note: As a kid, my dad would take us to rock shows. Like earth rocks, not the music. He had a collection of interesting minerals and rocks, as well as a handful of fossils that we would look through the glass of the display case at home. I was raised with a familiarity of petrified wood, how it's actually a rock and how it came into the world. I think I even had some as a kid. It might've been my favorite, but I could be making that up. I wonder if that's the awe-striking part of this park for some. Or if it's the fact that this desert was once a dense forest. That was it for me.

name: Saguaro National Park
note: On our drive from Dallas to San Diego, we intentionally went a bit out of the way to go to Carlsbad Caverns. That was fun and the natural stop felt like Tucson. Little did we know, Saguaro National Park is literally right in the middle of Tucson! Hello? Better yet, we went right in the middle of the blooming season for the saguaros, so we went at the perfect time of year. Who would've thought we'd visit two national parks on what first seemed like a chore of a drive?

name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
note: My dad grew up in Hawaii and he has this old story of his siblings going up to the eruption and playing near the lava in the 60s or 70s. Kilauea took a long while, but it became active again recently, spewing lava high into the air somewhat consistently. For my birthday, we came out and tried timing the trip. The first couple days were quiet, but we kept a close eye on the cameras. Come the day of my birthday, right as I wake up, the volcano erupts! What a fantastic birthday present.

name: Haleakala National Park
note: I was young when I went, long before the pin collection. As has become tradition, my dad and I left my mom and sister in the hotel room in ambitious pursuit of nature and adventure. A tired 12 year old me rose at 4am to drive up a mountain and watch the sunrise for a couple hours. The sights remain seared into my eyes. The greens and oranges of the valley, the neighboring islands faint, but solidly present in the distance. Was this where I fell in love with nature? Quite possibly.

name: Gateway Arch National Park
note: Everyone's favorite national park, so full of natural sights and greatness. This is also the first national park that I got to use my America the Beautiful pass at, and instead of saving $30 entering the park like at most places, I saved $5 for going up the arch. What a steal!

name: Zion National Park
note: I always knew I wanted to do the Utah national park loop ever since I moved to Vegas, but nothing really anchored that in as much as visiting Zion for the first time. The huge orange walls staring down upon you, that lay amidst already impressive structures but pounce just as you think that this is the best it gets. Everything about Zion wants to bring me back. Despite not having enough time off for the whole loop in one fell swoop, two Labor Days later is what it took to get to all five national parks.

name: Bryce Canyon National Park
note: Five Utah parks later and I believe that this is my favorite of the bunch. Zion has made a strong case, but something about the scratched earth of Bryce Canyon has a lot of staying power. The landscape is fantastic, being above and below. Hoodoo is fun to say which is a plus.

name: Arches National Park
note: Ran labor day back in 2026 with another great Utah park trip. Instead of spending the weekend at only one park, we managed three! Arches might be home to my favorite short hike thus far, the Double-O Arch. We got to scramble up some fun ledges and only got lost a couple times.

name: Canyonlands National Park
note: The island in the sky, to me, is similar to the Grand Canyon but in the opposite direction. At the Grand Canyon, you approach the ledge without really realizing how high up you are. Island in the sky, however, makes no secret about it. The name, the drive, everything about it. You drive all the way up and look all the way down.

name: Capitol Reef National Park
note: Labor Day 2026 featured one of my most ambitious drives yet. Unlike visiting Carlsbad Caverns, we opted for a long, double digit hours road trip simply because we wanted to drive that far. We started with sunrise at delicate arch, swung by Capitol Reef, drove across UT-12, decided not to go to Bryce Canyon, and finally landed at home 10 hours later. Somehow, some way, I'll make it to UT-95 next.

name: RLCS 21-22 Winter Major
note: The first live RLCS major back after COVID was in LA. I dragged some people to come with me. They bought the $80 tickets then complained about my cheering and joy.

name: RLCS 22-23 Winter Major
note: This blurb takes a massively different turn than you were probably thinking. This event is notable in my life because it was in my departure from the venue that I got to have my final conversation with my grandma. I left, I called, I cried, I cried some more, and returned to my friend. On the way home, she passed away and I cried again on the trolley.
